summary: PhysicsLabRecipe.objectGenome() has a small retained no-execute boundary gap independent of the active scale-overflow review. The exported helper accepts a statically typed ObjectGenomeKey but performs OBJECT_GENOMES[key] and then interpolates the original caller value in the unknown-key assert before runtime-proving that the key is a primitive string. A metatable-backed table passed through any/dynamic code can therefore execute caller __tostring during fail-closed rejection. Recommend a bounded follow-on source leaf after the current physics-geometry line completes: primitive-type-check the key before lookup/diagnostics, keep unknown-string rejection generic/safe, and add a zero-metamethod-execution regression while preserving every known canonical genome mapping.
evidence: PR #423 exact head aad25ec8aeef7437ad0938ead2259a6e39f3670f retains PhysicsLabRecipe.objectGenome(key) as: local genome = OBJECT_GENOMES[key]; assert(genome ~= nil, `unknown Physics Lab ObjectGenome key {key}`); return genome. There is no runtime primitive-string check before interpolation.

The same repository has already established this threat model in Physics Lab runtime hardening: retained PR #310 explicitly adds primitive-string checks so hostile non-string entity/schema keys cannot execute __tostring during diagnostics. The objectGenome helper remains outside that runtime input preflight.
